verdicts.strongest_argument: The substance is fully public and the tape already paid for it. Nanox pre-announced Q2 revenue of 'approximately $4.0 to $4.1 million' and the $31.4m 6/30 cash balance in a 6-K on 2026-07-23, and the same document introduced the going-concern language; the release was carried on StockTitan and MarketScreener the same day and the baseline records a -8.01% move on 2026-07-23. So the number that will print tomorrow has been known for seven weeks and cost the stock 8% on the day it became known. What survives is narrow and mechanical: two aggregators (FXEmpire $5.49m/5 analysts, MarketBeat via dailypolitical.com $5.376m on 2026-09-06) still carry a stale pre-announcement consensus, so wire copy tomorrow will read '~26% revenue miss'. I confirmed that stale consensus is itself published, which means the headline is foreseeable to anyone reading a preview — it is a print-day artefact on a $65m retail-heavy nano-cap, not new information about the company. I also checked the framing: $4.0-4.1m is a sequential decline (Q1 2026 revenue was $4,311k per the Q1 6-K exhibit) but a +33-37% y/y increase against $3.0m in Q2 2025, and the y/y framing is the one the company's own release will lead with. The claim is factually right and materially over-weighted.

Wire coverage of the same preliminary Q2 revenue guidance, with the teleradiology/systems/AI split.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The pre-announcement date carries a recorded -8.01% move (2026-07-23, the densest single non-print reaction in the recorded series other than the two real earnings dates), which is the market paying for this revenue number when it became known. No option chain and no skew, so nothing further can be said about what is priced for tomorrow.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the pre-announced range was a floor and the reported figure lands materially below $4.0m, or that a sell-side note has re-based estimates so no 'miss' headline is generated at all.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The existence of the impairment review is published twice in primary filings and once on the wire, but the magnitude genuinely is not drawn out anywhere I could find. The 2026-07-23 6-K already said Nanox was evaluating 'impairment charges relating to certain long-lived assets and/or goodwill'; the 2026-08-06 6-K — which I fetched and which is primarily a registered direct offering of 8m units at $1.00 — broadens it to 'a comprehensive impairment assessment across all of its assets, including but not limited to long-lived assets and goodwill' with results that 'may differ, potentially materially'. That broadening sits inside an offering document and I found no article that picked it up. The carrying values are correct: I verified from the Q1 2026 6-K exhibit that intangible assets net are $57,364k and property and equipment net $30,551k at 2026-03-31 (goodwill is only $316k, so the hunter's $88.0m is right and its composition is intangibles plus PP&E, not goodwill). Against that, three things pull the number up. First, precedent: the company already took a $17.5m non-cash impairment on the Korean chip line in Q4 2025, reported 2026-04-20, so the market has seen this movie. Second, the arithmetic already argues the market has done the writedown itself — total shareholders' equity was $126.3m at 3/31 against a ~$65m market cap, i.e. the equity trades at roughly half book, and even a full $88m impairment leaves ~$38m of net assets, below where the shares are marked. A non-cash charge that only confirms a discount the tape already applies is not the same as new information. Third, it does not create a listing trigger: post-impairment equity of ~$38m still clears Nasdaq's $10m equity standard, and the sub-$1 bid price problem exists independently at $0.8676. What is left unpriced is the headline shock of a $100m+ GAAP net loss line landing in a first quarter signed off by a CFO who started 2026-08-01 (Guy Nathanzon, announced 2026-04-14) — a real kitchen-sink risk, but a second-order one.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-08-06 filing date carries a recorded +2.00% and the following session +0.47%, so the broadened impairment language produced no visible reaction — though that is confounded by the concurrent $8m offering at $1.00. No option chain, so no skew statement is available about how much downside is being paid for.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published article or sell-side note between 2026-07-23 and today that puts a dollar figure on the impairable carrying value, which would take this to 80+; conversely, confirmation that the assessment also covers capitalised deferred costs or triggers a covenant would push it below 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The factual identification is correct and I verified both dates independently — 2026-04-20 bmo was the Q4/FY2025 release and 2026-06-25 bmo was the Q1 2026 release, and NNOX closed 2026-06-25 at $0.8697, down ~44.6%, cross-checked against the stockanalysis.com history table where 2026-06-26 closes at $1.09 (+23.95%) off that base. So the baseline's -44.01% and -24.39% really are earnings reactions and the six-day cadence inference really is wrong. But that is a correction to our own priors, not information the market lacks: a two-observation reaction history is the tape, visible on every chart, and is as close to 100% public as anything in this brief. Worse, the base rate the claim wants to extract does not survive its own evidence. Both declines were caused by information arriving for the first time — the 2026-04-20 print introduced the $17.5m Korea impairment and a wider loss, and the 2026-06-25 print withdrew the $35m FY2026 revenue target and introduced substantial-doubt going-concern language. Every one of those four shocks has already been disclosed ahead of tomorrow, and revenue and cash have been pre-announced besides, so extrapolating '2-for-2 double-digit declines' onto a print whose contents are largely known is a category error rather than a base rate. The instability is visible too: the -44% was almost entirely retraced within two sessions (+23.95% then +11.01%). I am scoring this as near-fully priced on market-information grounds while noting it is nonetheless the most operationally useful of the four for the pipeline's own baseline hygiene.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: none — per the brief's warning the recorded 6.52% median and 3-of-8 up-count are not an earnings base rate, and I am not using them. The only tape facts I rely on are the two verified print-day closes, which are public and therefore not a statement about anything unpriced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This finding is close to self-refuting as a novelty claim: its own thesis is that the four downside catalysts are already disclosed, and every single component I checked is a globenewswire press release or a filed 6-K, which is the definition of published. Guidance withdrawal and going-concern doubt: Q1 release, 2026-06-25. Korea restructuring and the $17.5m charge: Q4 2025 release, 2026-04-20, with the release itself stating total charges of ~$18.0m so only ~$0.5m remains. Q2 revenue and the $31.4m cash balance: 6-K, 2026-07-23. The positive-news cadence is three globenewswire items on 2026-08-10 (Intel Core Ultra / OpenVINO), 2026-08-18 (Vertec exclusive UK reseller for HealthOST) and 2026-09-04 (Associated X-Ray Imaging, New England) — all wire-distributed and all picked up by StockTitan. The 2026-09-17 meeting to lift authorised shares to 150m and grant CEO RSUs is in the proxy 6-K and has been written up by TipRanks and by StockTitan under the headline 'warns on cash runway before vote to boost share pool', so even the sceptical framing of the vote is on the wire. And the tape shows the cadence being paid for: the 5-day run-up is +7.51% into the print against -18.54% over 20 days, which is exactly the shape you would expect if the 9/4 distributor release was bid. The residual I will credit is the synthesis — that pre-announcing revenue, cash and going concern strips this print of the specific shocks that caused the last two collapses, leaving the impairment as the only live unknown — plus the incentive argument that management wants a clean tape two sessions before a majority vote it needs. That synthesis is an inference, not a fact, and I could not find it drawn out anywhere; it is why this is 79 rather than 92. Note it also directly cannibalises NNOX#0 and NNOX#2: if the de-risking argument holds, the revenue miss is stale and the two-print base rate is not transferable.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: 5-day run-up +7.51% against a 20-day of -18.54% and a spot of $0.8676 — the recent bid is consistent with the 9/4 distributor release already being paid for. No option chain and no skew, so there is no direct read on whether the market is discounting the de-risking argument.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the 2026-09-17 vote required a supermajority or a contested outcome that made a clean print materially valuable to management, or if any of the three commercial agreements carried disclosed minimum committed dollar volumes large against a $16m annualised revenue base, this would drop toward 50.

interactions: Three of the four rest on the same document. NNOX#0 (pre-announced Q2 revenue), NNOX#1 (impairment evaluation) and NNOX#3 (revenue, cash and going concern already disclosed) all trace to the 2026-07-23 6-K, which pre-announced revenue of ~$4.0-4.1m, $31.4m of 6/30 cash, substantial-doubt going-concern language AND the impairment evaluation in one release — the same release that carries a recorded -8.01% reaction. That single -8% is the market's one visible payment for this cluster, and it has to be shared across all three. NNOX#3 is the direct mirror of NNOX#0 and NNOX#2 and undercuts both: if the four shocks are already out, then the 'guaranteed 26% miss' is a stale-aggregator artefact rather than news, and the 2-for-2 double-digit-decline base rate is not transferable because both prior declines were caused by first-time disclosures that have now been made. NNOX#3 also cites the 2026-04-20 Korea $17.5m charge as de-risking while NNOX#1 treats the same event's successor assessment as the live risk — they are consistent only if the new assessment is materially broader than the Korea line, which the 2026-08-06 language ('all of its assets') does support. Finally, NNOX#2 is not a claim about the company at all but a correction to our own baseline; scoring it as near-fully priced does not mean it is worthless, and the pipeline should fix the six-day cadence inference regardless of the score.
